summary:
We have developed an interactive STEM game focused on managing a base on the Moon or Mars. Titled "Space Base Commander," the game challenges students to manage limited resources—such as energy, water, oxygen, and food—while balancing life support systems, radiation shielding, power generation, and food production. Since systems like solar panels, hydroponic farming, water recycling, and shelters are interconnected, students can observe the impact that every decision has on the base as a whole.

The project addresses the issue where engineering choices in space-themed educational content are either overly simplified or rendered too difficult for students to grasp. By encountering scenarios such as dust storms, solar radiation, and system failures, students develop skills in risk management, resource allocation, and problem-solving. In this way, abstract STEM concepts are transformed into the concrete decision-making processes required for an actual mission.

This approach is significant because it enables students to learn scientific thinking, establish intersystem relationships, and experience the consequences of engineering decisions. The game serves as a digital learning tool that makes education in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) engaging, accessible, and enduring.
details:
Project Details: Space Base Commander

Space Base Commander is an interactive STEM game that allows students to experience engineering decisions encountered on a real space mission by managing a Moon or Mars base. In the game, students try to ensure the safety of the crew and the success of the mission by balancing interconnected systems such as life support, radiation shield, energy production and food production.

How Does It Work?

The player manages limited energy, water, oxygen and food resources. It is necessary to establish the right balance between components such as solar panels, hydroponic agricultural unit, water recycling system, shelter and radiation shield Dec. For example, investing in a hydroponic system to produce more food increases energy and water consumption, which requires strengthening energy production.

As the mission progresses, events such as dust storms, solar radiation, equipment failure and resource shortages occur. Also in the game, aliens come to the base from time to time and offer water, supplies or other resources to the student. This situation allows the student to evaluate new opportunities in resource management and make strategic decisions. Each decision affects the resource balance and crew health, so the student can directly observe the consequences of their decisions.

The Benefits It Provides

The project enables students to learn about space, energy, ecology, and engineering in an enjoyable environment. Students gain skills in understanding inter-system relationships, using resources efficiently, conducting risk analysis, and making strategic decisions.

Students also develop problem-solving and critical thinking skills. The game can be made suitable for all age groups with different difficulty levels, so that it becomes an educational tool that can be used for both elementary school students and high school students.

Intended Effect

The main purpose of the project is to make space-themed STEM education more concrete, understandable, and engaging. Students understand that a space base is not only a technological system but also requires planning, resource management, and decision-making. This experience aims to increase students' interest in science and engineering.

In the long term, the project may become widespread as a digital educational material that can be used in science classes, science festivals and STEM workshops in schools. It provides the basis for future engineers and scientists by enabling students to think through scenarios similar to real world problems.

The Tools and Technologies Used

The project was developed as a web-based application. HTML, CSS and JavaScript were used for the interface design. Game logic, resource calculations, system interactions and event management are encoded with JavaScript. Visual elements, icon sets and color palette are prepared with a simple and modern design that students can easily understand.

During the development process, simple and intuitive interface principles were taken into account to improve the user experience. The game running through the browser allows students to access it without installing additional software. In this respect, the project can be easily used in environments with limited technical infrastructure in schools.

Creativity and Team Approach

The most creative aspect of our project is that it gamifies complex engineering concepts to enable active student participation. The systems, which are inspired by real task scenarios, make it possible for the student not only to acquire information, but also to make decisions and see the results. For example, strengthening the radiation shield may increase crew health but also raise energy consumption; the student learns to strike this balance. The aliens' provision of water and material support adds an element of imagination and surprise to the game, making the learning experience more enjoyable.

As a team, we took into account the following factors:

1-To design a simple and visual interface for students to understand

2-To reflect real engineering principles without being overly complicated

3-To clearly show the influence of resources on each other in the game

4-To ensure being fun and instructive at the same time

5-To offer difficulty levels suitable for different age groups

6-To improve the student's problem solving skills with unexpected events

7-Adding surprise and creativity to resource management through aliens

8-Choosing a web-based solution to increase accessibility
